subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Signaling Theory
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Signaling Theory.

hook.text: A peacock's tail is a handicap. It slows escape from predators. But hens see it as proof of fitness.

buildup.text: Spence applied signaling to economics. A college degree signals ability even if the degree teaches nothing job-relevant.

discovery.text: Costly signals are credible because fakers cannot afford them. The expense filters pretenders from the genuine.

twist.text: If degrees were free, they would signal nothing. The cost of the signal is what makes it informative to employers.

climax.text: Resumes, warranties, and brand spending all work as costly signals. They say: I can afford to waste this if I am lying.

punchline.text: The signal works because it is expensive to fake.

quiz.question: Why are costly signals credible?
options: Because people trust expensive things automatically
Because fakers cannot afford the cost, filtering them out

details.summary: Signaling theory explains how people convey hidden information through costly actions. A college degree signals intelligence not just through education but because completing it is costly enough that less capable individuals cannot easily fake the signal.
details.whyItMatters: Signaling drives enormous economic activity: education spending, luxury purchases, corporate charity, and job market behavior. Understanding that signals must be costly to be credible explains why seemingly wasteful spending persists.
takeaways: Effective signals must be costly enough that they cannot be easily faked
Education partly signals ability rather than teaching useful skills
Luxury spending signals resources by demonstrating ability to waste

faq.question: Is a college degree primarily a signal or an education?
faq.answer: Michael Spence argued that much of education's labor market value comes from signaling. Completing a difficult degree demonstrates intelligence, persistence, and conformity. The fact that employers value degrees regardless of major supports the signaling interpretation.

faq.question: Why must signals be costly to work?
faq.answer: If a signal were free, everyone would use it regardless of whether they had the underlying quality. A fitness display only signals health because unhealthy individuals cannot fake it. Cost creates credibility by making the signal too expensive for fakers.
